agent.job: identification beside a word that is always rendered
agent.source: valorant-api.com, serving Riot Games' own artwork

weapon.job: one distinct silhouette per breakdown row, on a theme-invariant plate
weapon.source: valorant-api.com, serving Riot Games' own artwork

rank.job: recognition beside the division word, which is what encodes
rank.source: valorant-api.com, serving Riot Games' own artwork

mwpa.label: MWPA
mwpa.definition: Match win probability added. A player's round credits, each centered on the mean credit of everyone else who played that round, each multiplied by the round's marginal match value, and summed. A value of +62.00% is six tenths of a match win added.

impact.label: Impact per match
impact.definition: MWPA divided by the matches the player was in: the share of a match win their credited actions are worth, per match played. +6.4% is six extra wins per hundred matches. It is the per-100-rounds rate rescaled by the player's own rounds per match, a positive constant, so the BCa endpoints carry across unchanged and so does `covers_zero`.

rate.label: MWPA per 100 rounds
rate.definition: MWPA divided by the rounds the player was credited in, times 100. It is the estimator's own unit; the four are ranked on `impact`.
rate.unit: match win probability points per 100 rounds

lo.label: Interval low
lo.definition: Lower bound of the 95.0% BCa bootstrap interval, from 100,000 replicates at seed 20260726, resampling whole matches so that rounds from one match move together.
lo.unit: match win probability points per 100 rounds

hi.label: Interval high
hi.definition: Upper bound of the same interval as `lo`. The width is the honest statement about this exposure; it is not an error bar to be squinted past.
hi.unit: match win probability points per 100 rounds

covers_zero.label: Interval covers zero
covers_zero.definition: True when the interval spans zero, meaning this exposure does not separate the number from no effect at all. Check `matches` first: a cell whose rounds all come from one match has a zero-width interval and this flag carries no information there.

total.label: Season total
total.definition: Signed sum of the player's MWPA across the act, in matches added rather than a rate.

rounds.label: Rounds
rounds.definition: Rounds in which the player carries at least one eligible ledger row. A player absent from a round has no row and contributes no zero.

matches.label: Matches
matches.definition: Distinct matches contributing at least one round. This is also the number of clusters the bootstrap has to resample, which is what sets the interval width.

rank.label: Rank
rank.definition: Position among the four when sorted by `impact`, best first. Ranking is on by decision rather than because the data separates the players; the interval on each card is what keeps the ordering honest.

thin.label: Thin cell
thin.definition: True when the cell has fewer than 20 rounds. The rate and interval are still shown. The flag says the exposure is small, not that the number is wrong.

share.label: Share of ledger
share.definition: The component's share of the player's total absolute credit across the components the rail draws — the duel as one row, then plant, defuse, the alive clock and the lobby adjustment. It describes what the ledger is made of, not how much of the headline the component explains.

cumulative.label: Running total
cumulative.definition: MWPA summed over every match up to and including this one, in match order. The tracker divides it by `i` + 1, the matches played to that point, which is what makes each line end on that player's `impact`, the number written at the end of the line.

exposure.label: Exposure
exposure.definition: The rounds behind a cell, said against `gate.exposure_threshold_rounds` — the rounds a leverage-weighted rate needs before its interval can exclude zero. It is the answer to why an interval is as wide as it is, and it is printed instead of an interval on a cell whose rounds all come from one match.

null.label: The null
null.definition: The value that means no claim. It is +0.000 in a rate and 50.0% on the match win probability curve, and it is drawn as one continuous rule at full strength: every quantity on this site is read as a departure from it, or as a failure to depart from it.

kills_per_match.label: Kills
kills_per_match.definition: Kills per match played, from the platform's own box score, averaged over the act matches this player appears in. It is a count and not an estimate: there is no interval on it and the null rule does not apply to it.

deaths_per_match.label: Deaths
deaths_per_match.definition: Deaths per match played, on the same denominator as kills.

assists_per_match.label: Assists
assists_per_match.definition: Assists per match played, on the same denominator as kills. An assist splits 0.20 of a kill's credit in the ledger; here it is only counted.

rounds_per_match.label: Rounds
rounds_per_match.definition: The rounds this player was credited in, divided by their matches. This is what a match means for them, and it is the positive constant that turns the estimator's per-100-rounds rate into the impact per match at the top of the card.

card_agents.label: Most-played agents
card_agents.definition: The agents this player picked most, counted in MATCHES, because an agent is chosen once per match. A player with fewer than `gate.card_top_n` agents shows only what they have; nothing is padded.

card_weapons.label: Most-used guns
card_weapons.definition: The round-start primaries this player held most, counted in ROUNDS, because a gun is chosen once per round. `gate.free_pistol` is excluded: everybody starts a pistol round holding it, so its count measures how many pistol rounds the act contained rather than anything about the player.

leverage.label: Round leverage
leverage.definition: The swing L = P(match win | this round won) - P(match win | this round lost), at the score entering the round, from the exact race-to-13 recursion with win-by-two overtime. Bounded by 0.5, which is its value at 12-12.
leverage.unit: match win probability per round win probability

li.label: Leverage index
li.definition: The round's leverage divided by the act mean, so 1.00x is an ordinary round and 3.05x is one that mattered three times as much. It is a display index and nothing else: L is what multiplies a credit, and dividing by it was the error this project ruled out rather than a second way to weight.
li.unit: multiples of the act mean leverage

mean_leverage.label: Mean leverage
mean_leverage.definition: The mean of L over every round-player in the act. It exists to index leverage for display and is never multiplied into a credit.
mean_leverage.unit: match win probability per round win probability

confidence.label: Confidence level
confidence.definition: The nominal coverage of every interval on this site. One number, one bootstrap, one seed: a headline, a two-round weapon cell and a synergy pair are all drawn from the same replicates and are therefore comparable to each other.

wp_series.label: Match win probability curve
wp_series.definition: The focal side's match win probability as one continuous line that moves inside a round rather than once at each boundary. With the score at (a, b) and the focal side holding round win probability q, the match probability is W(a, b+1) + q x L(a, b), so the curve is the round model the ledger already produces, mapped onto the match by that round's own leverage. Its slope is the leverage, which is why a node's vertical move is the same number as that event's match impact rather than a second version of it.

p.label: Match win probability
p.definition: The focal side's probability of winning the match at one point on the curve, given the score and the state of the round in progress.

q.label: Round win probability
q.definition: The focal side's probability of winning the round in progress. It is the round-level quantity the ledger is built on; the curve is this number mapped onto the match.

dp.label: Move
dp.definition: The change in match win probability from the previous node. On an `action` node this is exactly that event's raw match impact, because the curve's slope is the round's leverage: a kill that moves the line 3.4 points moved the match 3.4 points. On the other three kinds it belongs to nobody, and `kind` says which.

kind.label: Node kind
kind.definition: Which of four different claims a point on the curve is making: `round_start`, `clock`, `action` or `terminal`. They are drawn differently because only one of them is attributable to a player.

kind_round_start.label: Round start
kind_round_start.definition: The buy is known and the model prices the round before anyone has acted. It is usually the largest move nobody made: round-start round win probability has a standard deviation of 0.153 across the act, so an eco round opens with the match already leaning away. It belongs to the economy, never to a player, and carries no MWPA.

kind_clock.label: Clock
kind_clock.definition: Probability drifting between credited actions as the round ages. This is the alive-clock component of the ledger, split across each side's survivors.

kind_action.label: Action
kind_action.definition: An event with a time on it: a kill, a plant, a defuse, a revive, a spike detonation or an expired timer. The line's vertical move at one is that event's match impact, in match win probability points. Only the first three are credit types — the rest move the curve and are credited to nobody, which is why an action row can name an actor and still put nothing in that player's ledger.

kind_terminal.label: Terminal
kind_terminal.definition: The round resolves. The gap from the last action to here is the model's own calibration error at the terminal, which the ledger books to a team side rather than to a player. It is drawn rather than smoothed away.

x.label: Position in the match
x.definition: Where a node sits along the match axis: the round number minus one, plus the share of that round's own clock elapsed. Whole numbers are round boundaries, so every round is the same width however long it took.

t.label: Time into the round
t.definition: Milliseconds from the start of the round to the node. The round's last event sets the horizon its x position is measured against.

wp_before.label: Match WP entering the round
wp_before.definition: The focal side's match win probability at the score entering the round, before the round is priced. It is the value the curve arrives at from the previous round.

wp_after.label: Match WP after the round
wp_after.definition: The same quantity once the round has resolved. This is a reconciliation and not an identity: the last round's value is a structural probability read off the score, not the result, and the two differ often enough that asserting equality would fail.

p_before.label: Round WP before the action
p_before.definition: The focal side's round win probability immediately before a credited action.

p_after.label: Round WP after the action
p_after.definition: The focal side's round win probability immediately after the same action. The difference between the two is what the ledger pays out.

delta.label: Action swing
delta.definition: The action's move in round win probability, before leverage. Multiplying it by the round's leverage is what turns it into match units.

terminal_type.label: Ended by
terminal_type.definition: How the round resolved, as the platform recorded it: an elimination, a defuse, a detonation, or a timer running out.

attack_mwpa.label: Attack MWPA
attack_mwpa.definition: The player's MWPA in this match summed over the rounds their team attacked.

defense_mwpa.label: Defense MWPA
defense_mwpa.definition: The player's MWPA in this match summed over the rounds their team defended.

duel_credit.label: Duel credit
duel_credit.definition: Kill credit and death debit as one signed row: what the player's duels were worth net, after paying for the ones they lost. The two are the two ends of one event, and they are also an order of magnitude longer than every other component and pointed opposite ways — drawn apart they set an axis on which plant, defuse and the clock have no visible length. Resampled as a single column, never added out of two intervals: within a round the two are strongly negatively correlated, so their widths do not add.

kill_credit.label: Kill credit
kill_credit.definition: Probability gained at kills the player made. An unassisted kill pays the killer in full; an assisted one pays 0.80 to the killer and splits 0.20 across the assists. That split is a construction convention, not an estimate.

death_debit.label: Death debit
death_debit.definition: Probability lost when the player died, debited in full to the victim. It is typically the largest single piece of a player's absolute ledger.

plant.label: Plant
plant.definition: Probability gained by planting the spike, paid to the planter.

defuse.label: Defuse
defuse.definition: Probability gained by defusing, paid to the defuser.

alive_clock.label: Alive clock
alive_clock.definition: The probability drift between events, split equally across each side's survivors. It is bookkeeping for who was present while the state aged, not a measure of survival skill.

lobby_adjustment.label: Lobby adjustment
lobby_adjustment.definition: The centering itself, booked as its own row: the mean credit of everyone else in the round, which no single credit type owns. With it the components sum to the headline exactly.

agent.label: Agent
agent.definition: The agent the player picked. Only the player with several hundred rounds on each of three agents has cells here that can be told apart; for everyone else this table is one usable row or none.

map.label: Map
map.definition: The map played. Seven of the pool's thirteen appear in this act, which spreads a player's matches thin enough that most map cells are a handful of games.

side.label: Side
side.definition: Attack or defense, from the player's team's point of view in that round. Sides swap at the half and again each round in overtime.

buy_class.label: Buy class
buy_class.definition: The team's round-start loadout band, in credits: eco below 5,000, light from 5,000 to 12,500, half from 12,500 to 20,000, full from 20,000. The cut points come from this corpus's own loadout distribution rather than Counter-Strike convention.

weapon.label: Weapon
weapon.definition: The player's round-start primary. Anything with fewer than 10 rounds is folded into `Other` rather than emitted as a tail of one-round cells.

key.label: Cell
key.definition: The value of the breakdown dimension this row covers.

partner_short.label: Partner
partner_short.definition: The other player in an ordered synergy pair. The row is the subject's own MWPA over the rounds this partner also played.

partner_name.label: Partner name
partner_name.definition: The partner's Riot id. Only the four consented players are ever named.

shared_matches.label: Shared matches
shared_matches.definition: Matches in which both players of the pair appear.

shared_rounds.label: Shared rounds
shared_rounds.definition: Rounds in which both players of the pair carry a ledger row. This is the exposure the pair's interval is drawn from.

score.label: Score
score.definition: Final rounds won, the four players' team first.

won.label: Result
won.definition: Whether the four players' team won the match.

started_at.label: Started
started_at.definition: Match start time as the platform reported it, in UTC. Matches are ordered by it everywhere on the site.

match_id.label: Match
match_id.definition: The platform's match identifier, and the join key between every file in this payload.

focal.label: Focal players
focal.definition: Which of the four played in this match. Everyone else in it is a match-scoped pseudonym.

i.label: Match index
i.definition: Zero-based position of the match in the player's own chronological order. It is not the tracker's x — that is the act's shared match order, so four series with 8, 32, 60 and 8 matches sit on one timeline. `i` is the denominator: `cumulative` over `i` + 1 is the player's running `impact`.

short.label: Short name
short.definition: The player's slug, used for file names and links.

puuid.label: Player id
puuid.definition: The player's stable identifier. It is stable only for these four; every other player in the corpus is re-pseudonymized per match.

tier.label: Division
tier.definition: The competitive division the platform had the player at when this match was played. It is per match, so a player has a path across the act rather than a rank. A null means no rank had been issued yet, which is a measurement and not a missing value.

rank_track.label: Rank trajectory
rank_track.definition: One step per match, in the player's own match order: the division held, its position on `gate.tier_order`, and whether a rank existed at all. This is the only source the trajectory figure draws from, and its `ordinal` is the only number allowed to be a y value there.

ordinal.label: Ladder position
ordinal.definition: One-based position on `gate.tier_order`, which is the platform's ladder with its unranked state removed. The platform's own enum numbers the unranked state zero on the same scale as the divisions; plotting that would put a player who has no rank yet below the bottom division, so this site does not carry it.

state.label: Rank state
state.definition: `ranked` or `placement`. In placement the platform had issued no rank, so there is no division, no ladder position and no axis to draw one against.

ladder.label: Ladder summary
ladder.definition: First and last division of the act, the highest and lowest held, how many matches were played before a rank existed, and how many times the division moved up and down between consecutive ranked matches.

lobby_tiers.label: Lobby divisions
lobby_tiers.definition: The range of divisions in this match's lobby, and how many of the ten had no rank issued yet. A lobby is not division-homogeneous, which is the one thing about divisions that a match page can answer.

cav.text: Every number here is act e11a4 alone — 100 matches, 2,046 rounds — with nothing pooled across acts.

65 of these matches were priced inside the model release, each by a fold fit without it. 35 were collected after the release was cut, and cross-fitting keeps its predictions but not its models, so those are priced by a refit on the release's own core at the parameters all five folds already chose. Neither kind was in the training data of the model that scored it; what differs is that one model saw four fifths of the corpus and the other saw all of it, worth a mean 0.6% of round win probability across the act's states.

23 rounds in this act ended in a surrender. A surrendered round is awarded, not played — no events, no kills — so it is outside every number here, while the rounds played before it stay in: they ran under a real race to 13, against a score nobody yet knew would be conceded. The scoreline on such a match is the played one, and the round count reconciles against it.

The four are ordered on impact per match because that decision was taken for this site, not because the data separates them. All four intervals cover zero. No page prints a rank number any more: what survives is the order the four are listed in, on the season tracker's legend and in the columns of the match cross-tab. Read that order as a sort, and the interval on each card as the result.

The attack/defense split cannot resolve at this exposure: it needs roughly 14,000 rounds at this credit variance and the act has 2,046. Both cells are published with their intervals; the width there is the sample, not the player.

Abilities do not exist in this data at any grain — four integers per player-match, null in every round record — so smokes, flashes and mollies are absent from every number here. Revives are UNCREDITED rather than absent: a revive is a timed event, so the curve moves under one and the round timeline prints that move beside whoever cast it, but revive is not one of the five credit types and no player's ledger carries it. The five are the whole ledger, and no cell renders a zero for utility.
Everyone but the four is a match-scoped pseudonym: the same person in two matches carries two unrelated names, and nothing here links them.

A noindex tag and a robots.txt keep this out of search results, which is not access control: the pages sit in a public repository, readable by anyone with the URL, including round-level detail on 807 players who did not consent to any of it. The point was raised before the build and the decision to publish was reaffirmed.

The 20-round floor marks a cell rather than suppressing it: below it a cell carries `thin` and still prints its number and interval. Per-round MWPA has a standard deviation of 0.0435 in this act, so a 20-round mean carries a pure-noise standard error of about 0.97 per 100 rounds against a spread between the four of 0.27 — read a thin cell as description, not estimate.

A breakdown cell with no rounds is omitted rather than emitted as zero, and the view renders that absence. A synergy pair is the exception: it keeps its row with a null rate, because two players never sharing a round is the finding.

Duel tags cover 10,232 of 10,310 earned rows; the missing 78, 0.8%, are 72 clutch_lost, 4 opening_death and 2 traded across 77 rounds. They have no round-player row to attach to, because the ledger scores nobody who was alive and produced no kill, death, plant, defuse or clock share — a clutch lost without firing is the modal case.

The bootstrap resamples whole matches, so a cell whose rounds all come from one match has a zero-width interval that reads as excluding zero and does not: one cluster, nothing for the resample to vary. Check `matches` before `covers_zero`.

A magnitude that rounds to zero at its own format is MEASURED, not missing: it prints as less than the smallest number that format can write, with no sign and no direction colour. The em dash stays reserved for the unmeasured, the middot for an exact zero.

The heaviest ink on every figure is the line at the value that means no claim, 50.0% on the match win probability curve, drawn as one unbroken element through a whole block rather than a tick per row. On the curve it sits UNDER the line, because a rule that heavy would otherwise erase the data wherever the match sat near even.

Kill credit and death debit are drawn as one signed row, the duel credit, and the two are still printed underneath it in words. The reason is legibility and it is arithmetic: the two are an order of magnitude longer than every other component and pointed opposite ways, so drawn apart they set an axis on which plant, defuse and the alive clock are a pixel each. They are also the two ends of one event — a duel resolves, somebody is paid, somebody is debited — so their sum is a quantity rather than a convenience. Its interval is resampled on the summed column and is not the two intervals added: within a round the two are strongly negatively correlated, so their widths do not add.

The most-used guns on a player card exclude the Classic. Every player starts every pistol round holding it, whatever they meant to buy, so a Classic count measures how many pistol rounds the act contained and not what this player chooses to hold. Nothing else is excluded, and the guns are counted in rounds rather than matches because a gun is a per-round choice.

The block at the top of a player page carries two registers and they are drawn apart. The impact per match is an estimate and it keeps its interval and its verdict against the null. The kills, deaths, assists, rounds, agents and guns beside it are counts: they happened, they carry no interval, and no null rule is drawn through them. A card that put a confidence band on a kill count would be claiming uncertainty about something nobody is uncertain about.

The five credit types decompose the raw ledger before the lobby centering, so a further row carries that centering and the rows sum to the headline exactly. Across the four the raw five sum to +5.1668 against a headline sum of +2.8829, and the lobby adjustment is the -2.2839 between them.

The curve steps at a round boundary and the step is real: the match model runs every future round at a constant win probability of 0.5, so a boundary is the score talking, and the round-start node then moves it to the model's price on the round about to be played. Across the 2,046 rounds of this act the median step is 1.5 match win probability points and the largest is 10.9; neither end of it is a player.

Weighting each round by its marginal match value widens every interval rather than narrowing it: the rounds needed to exclude zero rise from about 546 to about 726. Of the four, martin and snorlax clear that threshold; the rest do not.

The buy classes are cut from this corpus's own team-loadout distribution, not from Counter-Strike convention. Eco rounds are won 42.2% of the time in this act, against roughly one in thirty in professional Counter-Strike, which is direct evidence that the imported cut points describe a different game.

Synergy is ordered: each row is the subject's own MWPA over the rounds a given partner also played, not a joint estimate, so the two directions of a pairing are different numbers. martin and snorlax are the only pairing with real shared exposure, at 1,097 shared rounds; themarias and trzzcko never shared a round in this act, and that cell is null, not zero.

MWPA is a descriptive allocation of modelled probability movement, not a causal player effect. The model behind it carries no player, team or lobby term, so every credit is a residual against a baseline pooled across ranks.

A player's first 5 act matches are played before the platform has issued a rank: not a missing value and not a zero, but the measured answer that no division existed yet. Verified rather than assumed — 144 of the 811 act players who have such a match carry it as a strict prefix, with no counterexamples.

The ladder is a second instrument and it is not measuring this: over the 186 focal player-matches with at least 5 ranked others in the lobby, the lobby's mean division correlates with that match's MWPA at r = +0.024, with the lobby adjustment at r = +0.150, and with that adjustment as a rate at r = +0.115. Lobbies are not division-homogeneous either — the median spread inside one is 4 divisions and the widest is 8.

No picture here is a measurement, because of where they are put: three families ship — 29 agent portraits, 11 division badges, 19 weapon silhouettes — each beside a word that is always rendered, and the header control removes all 59 files at once, so flipping it costs recognition and not one fact. What clears the 3:1 mark floor is the 1-pixel box around each picture, at 3.42:1 worst, not the picture inside it — of the 29 portraits only 6 clear that floor on every surface they land on.

The round ledger stays words: across 20,322 named cells Vandal alone is 33.3%, so an icon column there repeats and is texture rather than navigation. The silhouettes ship in the `by weapon` breakdown, where every row is a distinct weapon; a division badge ships only beside the division word and never in a cell carrying a player hue, because Riot's gold sits within OKLab ΔE 3.5 of one player's own hue; map art is refused. The player card is the one place the art is not eighteen pixels tall — everywhere else it rides inside a table row and the row's line box is the constraint, and a card is not a row, so the agents and the guns on it are drawn at the size the files actually are. Nothing else about them changes: the word is beside every picture, the weapon plate comes with the weapon art, and the header control still takes all of it away without losing a fact.

All three families are Riot Games' own artwork, fetched once from valorant-api.com and served from this directory: 29 agent portraits at 40 pixels square, 11 division badges at 48 square, and 19 weapon silhouettes 96 pixels wide, used under Riot's fan content policy. This site is not endorsed by or affiliated with Riot Games.

16.0% of this act's player-matches carry no division, and no badge ships for that state: Riot's enum puts `Unrated` at id 0 on the ladder that has Iron 2 at 4, which would draw the absence of a rank as a rung below the lowest one, and `Unrated` is also the name of a queue while all 100 of these matches are Competitive. It is the word `placement` everywhere it appears — not an em dash, which on this site means NOT MEASURED — and on the ladder it gets an empty slot in a dashed hairline.
